newsitem.title: UK: WH Smith gains in strong retail sector.
newsitem.headline: WH Smith gains in strong retail sector.

text.p: Shares in WH Smith Plc jumped on Friday in a firm retail sector, squeezed higher by a badly-handled "buy" order amid hopes for upbeat trading statements from leading retailers in coming weeks, traders said.

A trading statement today from privately-owned John Lewis Partnership also gave an upbeat picture on consumer activity, dealers said, with department store sales up 8.8 percent in the week to December 28 from the same period a year before.
WH Smith shares were up 22p at 543-1/2 by 1155 GMT in modest volume of 508,678 shares.

Other retail stocks were mostly higher with Kingfisher Plc up 9p at 635-1/2, Marks & Spencer Plc up 5-1/2p at 485-1/2, Boots Co Plc 15p firmer at 619, Thorn Plc up 17-1/2p at 277 and Storehouse Plc gaining 4p to 260-1/2. Dixons Group Plc was up 6-1/2p at 548.

Dixons is poised to kick off a round of Christmas trading statements from top retailers next week, potentially lifting a sector which lagged in recent weeks on fears that interest rate rises in 1997 would cap the recovery in consumer confidence. "The news from John Lewis was quite good and the trading statements should be OK," said one dealer.

Yesterday, jewellery retailer Goldsmiths Group Plc said like-for-like sales in the four weeks to December 28 rose 9.8 percent from the year before, calming fears that retail activity generally had been disappointing in the key Christmas period.
Traders also pointed out that WH Smith had been buoyed last month by reports that Boots had considered a bid for the stationery and book retailer.
